seo.title: Altrazen | Software studio
seo.description: We build websites, online products and mobile apps, and we look after software that other people built. Clear plans, fixed prices, and work you own from day one.

hero.headline: Software that keeps working.
hero.subheadline: We build websites, online products and mobile apps for businesses. We also take on software that already exists and has become risky to run.

positioning.heading: We are still here after launch
paragraphs: Most software does not fail on launch day. It fails slowly. A year later nobody can change anything without breaking something else, the person who understood it has left, and starting again begins to look cheaper than carrying on.

We build to avoid that ending, and we take on the businesses where it has already happened. The two halves feed each other. Fixing other people's software is the best possible education in what not to do in your own.

points.title: Built for whoever comes next
points.description: Written instructions, small changes that are easy to check, and decisions recorded with the reasoning behind them. If only one person can look after something, we have done our job badly.

points.title: Everything in your name
points.description: Your hosting, your web address, your app store listings, your accounts, from the first day. Leaving us should never be technically difficult, so we never make it so.

points.title: We say no early
points.description: If your project is too small for us, outside what we do well, or would be better solved without building software at all, you hear it on the first call and not three weeks in.

capabilities.heading: Four things, done properly
capabilities.description: A short list we know well, rather than a long one we would be learning at your expense.

flagship.heading: The software nobody wants to touch
flagship.description: When we look inside software that was built in a hurry, the same problems come up again and again. Every one of these is quiet until the day it is not.

findings.label: The keys are under the mat
findings.description: The passwords to your system are sitting somewhere anyone who goes looking can find them.

findings.label: There is no real backup
findings.description: Either nothing is being saved, or something is, and nobody has ever checked that it can actually be brought back.

findings.label: The lock is on the wrong side of the door
findings.description: The checks that decide who can see what happen on the customer's device, where a determined person can simply walk past them.

findings.label: Faults happen quietly
findings.description: Something goes wrong, nothing is recorded and nobody is told. Everything looks fine while orders or messages are being lost.

findings.label: There is no undo
findings.description: Changes go straight to your live site with no way to reverse them quickly, so a small mistake becomes an emergency.

findings.label: Everything is out of date
findings.description: The parts your software is built from are years behind, several have known weaknesses, and catching up is now a project in itself.

steps.title: Talk
steps.outcome: You tell us the problem. We tell you whether we are the right people, including when we are not.

steps.title: Plan
steps.outcome: A written plan: what we will build, what we will not, how long it takes, what it costs, and the risks we can already see.

steps.title: Build
steps.outcome: A working version on a private link every week, with a short written update. You watch it take shape.

steps.title: Hand over or continue
steps.outcome: Instructions and a walkthrough, then either your team runs it or we look after it. Both are fine.

standards.heading: What we hold ourselves to
standards.description: These are not ambitions. Each one is a rule we follow on every project, and each one costs us something.

items.title: Nothing goes live without an undo
items.description: Every change can be reversed in one step, and we test that before launch rather than during an emergency.

items.title: Passwords are never left in the open
items.description: Not anywhere, and not at any point in a project's history. Where we take over software and find them exposed, changing them is the first thing we do.

items.title: Every alert reaches a person
items.description: An alert that only appears on a screen nobody opens is not an alert. If it cannot reach someone, it does not count.

items.title: We test where failure costs money
items.description: Payments, signing in, and anything that saves customer information. We do not chase a tidy looking score that measures the wrong thing.

items.title: Everyone can use it
items.description: People using a keyboard, a screen reader or a small phone can use what we build. It is checked automatically, not left as a step that gets dropped when the date gets close.

items.title: We tell you about our own mistakes
items.description: Straight away, in plain language, with what we are doing about it. Finding out later from your customers is not something we will put you through.

whoWeAre.heading: Small, and growing carefully
paragraphs: Altrazen is a small studio, and that is a decision rather than a stage we are trying to grow out of. It means the people you speak to are the people doing the work, and nothing gets passed through someone who has never seen your project.
It also means we take on fewer projects at a time than a large agency, and we turn down work that is not a good fit. If you want a team that will tell you when the answer is no, that is the trade.

finalCta.heading: Tell us what you need
finalCta.description: Or what has already gone wrong. One conversation is usually enough to know whether we are the right studio, and we will tell you either way.
